description:
Found while running the full workspace suite on the maintainer's Windows box, 2026-07-27. NOT introduced by that session's work — kopitiam-semantic was not touched.

All 7 lsp_types::tests::definition_* tests fail, and they fail by producing NOTHING rather than something wrong:

  definition_parses_a_single_location_object            left: 0  right: 1
  definition_parses_a_location_array                    left: 0  right: 2
  definition_parses_a_location_link_array_...           left: 0  right: 1
  definition_link_falls_back_to_target_range_...        left: 0  right: 1
  definition_drops_a_non_file_uri_but_keeps_its_siblings left: 0  right: 1
  definition_converts_the_target_offset_from_each_wire_encoding  index out of bounds: len is 0 but index is 0
  definition_converts_an_offset_after_an_astral_emoji            index out of bounds: len is 0 but index is 0

Every parse yields an empty vec, so the two index-out-of-bounds panics are the same root cause showing a different face.

HYPOTHESIS (not yet confirmed): file:// URI -> path conversion on Windows. A 'file:///C:/foo/bar.rs' URI has a drive letter and a leading slash that unix-shaped parsing drops or rejects, so every location is discarded as non-file. The one test that ASSERTS a non-file URI gets dropped (definition_drops_a_non_file_uri_but_keeps_its_siblings) failing with left:0 right:1 fits exactly: the real one is being dropped too.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE TESTS: this is the code path behind kvim's <leader>gd / gr / hover. If it really is URI handling, go-to-definition is broken for every Windows user of kvim, not merely red in CI. Termux/Linux is unaffected, which is why this survived.

NEXT STEP: read crates/kopitiam-semantic/src/lsp_types.rs around lines 485-600 and check the uri->PathBuf conversion against 'file:///C:/...'.

notes.author: fifad@Teddy-Thinkpad
notes.content: CORRECTION to this bead's own diagnosis (fix landed in c587071). I claimed kvim go-to-definition was broken for every Windows user. WRONG — probed instead of trusting it: on Windows file:///tmp/lib.rs -> None (what the tests hit) but file:///C:/tmp/lib.rs -> C:\tmp\lib.rs and file:///c%3A/tmp/lib.rs -> c:\tmp\lib.rs both convert fine, and jdt:// correctly drops. Real rust-analyzer on Windows sends drive-letter URIs, so gd/gr/hover was never broken in production. The tests were unix-only by accident, hardcoding file:///tmp/... and asserting /tmp/..., which quietly made the definition suite Linux-only. THE REAL DEFECT, now fixed: to_file_path() needs a drive letter on Windows, so a genuine file: URI from a Linux/Termux/WSL/container server was dropped SILENTLY and indistinguishably from the jdt: case that is meant to be dropped. Reachable because KOPITIAM targets Windows and Termux together and the server need not run on the client's platform. uri_to_path now drops on SCHEME never on platform, percent-decodes the URI path when the native converter refuses, and refuses a non-empty host (UNC) rather than stripping it into a confidently wrong local path. 6 new tests pin both platforms, cfg-splitting expectations where platforms genuinely differ instead of weakening them. kopitiam-semantic: 10 failures -> 3, the 3 left are bd-cfu's. clippy -D warnings clean.

title: kopitiam-semantic: lsp_types definition parsing returns ZERO results on Windows (7 tests red)
